title: Inside CHANEL’s "Signes & Symboles" High Jewelry Collection

Story by Kate Granger, Editor of RUNWAY MAGAZINE. Photo Courtesy: CHANEL. Creation is a mystery, but for Gabrielle Chanel, it was primarily a declaration of absolute independence. She did not design her dresses; she cut them directly from the fabric. She did not follow the rigid, patriarchal laws of classical jewelry; she invented her own vocabulary, mixing the opulent weight of Byzantine artifacts with the humble talismans she collected like armor. With the unveiling of the “Signes & Symboles” High Jewelry Collection, the CHANEL Jewelry Creation Studio presents 85 masterful pieces that translate Mademoiselle’s inner cosmic landscapes into absolute material reality. This is not merely an exhibition of precious stones; it is an intellectual exercise in sacred geometry, where symmetry, contrast, and rare gemstones form a complex dialogue between the house’s four core pillars: the Camellia, the Star, the Sun, and the Lion. Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel 1937, Photo Roger Schall, Courtesy CHANEL Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel 1937, Photo Roger Schall, Courtesy CHANEL Les Imprimés: Fabric Woven from Light and Sapphires In a spectacular display of technical mastery, the collection’s first chapter treats hard gems as if they were fluid textiles. The iconic motifs are arranged in strict, rhythmic lines that mimic the drape of haute couture on the body. The Imprimé Lion Necklace: The true centerpiece of the collection effortlessly marries the Lion, Camellia, Star, and Sun into a single cascading V-line waterfall of pink and white gold threads. Custom-cut diamonds are set with nearly invisible prongs, creating a brilliant textile of light that culminates in an architectural marvel: a 20.66-carat octagonal-cut sapphire resting below a majestic, diamond-paved lion’s head. The Imprimé Émeraude Ring: A masterclass in color theory. Here, a magnificent 10.44-carat octagonal emerald is held by delicate pink gold prongs. Set upon an oval pedestal of custom-cut diamonds, it is flanked by two understated diamond camellias, proving that true elegance lies in calculated restraint. Le Lion Emblématique: Sovereignty in Onyx and Rubies First introduced to CHANEL High Jewelry in 2012, the lion—Gabrielle’s astrological birth sign—returns with an aggressive, contemporary sovereignty. The Lion Millénaire Necklace & Ring: This set explores the profound duality of texture and color. On the necklace, a diamond feline silhouette emerges as a crisp bas-relief against a stark onyx background, framing a fiery 6.12-carat octagonal ruby. The accompanying ring features a split personality: one head bears a 9.41-carat oval ruby, while the other mirrors the onyx and diamond bas-relief lion—an audacious design that offers stylistic transformation for the modern collector. The Lion Emblématique Brooch: Forgoing traditional constraints, this unapologetically bold piece frames a diamond lion’s head with a brilliant, sculptural mane composed of rubies, sapphires, emeralds, and turquoises. A fine yellow gold cord outlines its perfect symmetry, anchoring the chaotic explosion of color into a disciplined work of art. Les Bijoux Talismans: The Sacred Amulet Gabrielle Chanel surrounded herself with symbols because she believed in their protective, almost mystical forces. The Creation Studio honors this intimacy by carving amulets that function as modern protective armor. +————————–+————————————————————-+| Talisman Piece | Gemstone & Material Composition |+————————–+————————————————————-+| Talisman Graphique | Yellow gold, yellow sapphires, star engravings, and a || Necklace | 3.57-carat FL Type IIa emerald-cut diamond |+————————–+————————————————————-+| Talisman de Symboles | Tubular chain with pink gold, pink sapphires, diamonds, || Necklace
